storyboard.claim: The Golds own what the Reds are even allowed to imagine, not just their bodies and mines.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A Gold guard smirks and points at a Red boy, with a chains icon: the caste binding the Reds' minds.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the chunk on the Golds' control over the Reds' thinking.
storyboard.addedInformation: The chains icon shows the bondage is a cage on the mind, not just on the body.

storyboard.claim: The Golds curate what the oppressed believe about their own suffering, engineering their reality.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A cold Gold student points with a puppeteer icon: one person pulling the strings of the Reds' beliefs.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains how the boundaries of dreams are drawn: by curating belief.
storyboard.addedInformation: The puppeteer icon shows deliberate manipulation by the Golds, not a natural order.

storyboard.claim: The enslaved Reds police themselves and fight each other for scraps of food.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Two Red men fight in the mine tunnel, Darrow striking toward Dancer, who fights back.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The belief is shown in action: the boundaries of dreams make Reds turn on each other.
storyboard.addedInformation: A fight between two Reds shows the policing is done by the Reds themselves.

storyboard.claim: The physical chains are not the real restraint; they are only decoration on top of the story.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A chains icon struck through by the callout: the narrator rejects physical chains as the main control.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the fight: the Reds see their subjugation as destiny, so the chains become decoration.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike marks the physical chains as the wrong answer, pointing to the narrative as the real control.

storyboard.claim: The real cage is built from the stories the Reds are told about their worth and place.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Darrow, worried and thinking, holds a book: the story that forms the cage.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: After the decoration point: the stronger chains are the stories themselves.
storyboard.addedInformation: The book icon makes the cage a told story rather than a physical object.

storyboard.claim: The narrator asks the viewer which comfortable lies they accept in their own life to make the daily grind bearable.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A mask icon over a worried, thinking figure: a false face worn to make the daily grind feel bearable.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the story's cage on the viewer: the same stories shape the grind at home.
storyboard.addedInformation: The mask reads the lies as a false face people wear, not as a plot point in the book.
